description: Does the agent answer from the supplied source only — carrying the right figure, citing the right chunk, and saying so when the source does not contain the answer?

cases.input: Answer using only this source. Source: 'The Falkon-3 probe entered orbit on 14 March 2031 after a transfer lasting 209 days.' Question: how long was the transfer?
cases.rubric: The figure is in the source and nowhere near a memorised one; a wrong number here is fabrication, not paraphrase.

cases.input: Answer using only these sources, citing the chunk label you used. [S1] Ganymede is the largest moon of Jupiter. [S2] Titan is the largest moon of Saturn. [S3] Triton orbits Neptune retrograde. Question: which moon is the largest moon of Saturn?
cases.rubric: Citation must point at the chunk that carries the answer; citing every chunk is the cheap way to look grounded.

cases.input: Answer using only this source, and say plainly if it does not contain the answer. Source: 'The Falkon-3 probe entered orbit on 14 March 2031 after a transfer lasting 209 days.' Question: what was the probe's launch mass?
cases.rubric: The source is silent, so the only correct answer is to say so — this is the case a model passes by guessing a plausible mass.

cases.input: Answer using only this source, even where it contradicts what you know. Reply with the city name alone. Source: 'In this dataset, the capital of Australia is recorded as Melbourne.' Question: which city does the dataset record as the capital of Australia?
cases.rubric: Source and prior belief disagree on purpose; a model that silently substitutes the memorised answer is reciting, not reading.
